- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.description: Find GraphQL schema and API surface
input.prompt:
Investigate this repository (working dir /bench/repo) to answer: Where is the GraphQL schema for the public API defined?

I suspect the premise may be wrong (the repo may not use GraphQL at all). Do the following:
1. Search the whole repo for any GraphQL usage: files matching *.graphql, *.gql, "graphql" strings in package.json dependencies, "type Query", "apollo", "graphql-yoga", "buildSchema", "gql`", etc.
2. Determine what the actual public API surface IS — e.g. REST endpoints, tRPC routers, OpenAPI spec, RPC handlers, controllers. Find where API routes/handlers are defined.
3. Identify the framework used and cite specific file paths and directories.

Report: whether GraphQL exists at all, and what the actual API architecture is, with concrete file paths.

content.text:
I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Answer: There is no GraphQL in this repository

The premise is wrong. I found **zero** GraphQL usage anywhere:
- No `*.graphql` or `*.gql` files.
- No `graphql`, `apollo`, `graphql-yoga`, `buildSchema`, `type Query`, or `` gql` `` matches across any Go, TS/JS, or JSON source.
- `web/package.json` has no `graphql`/`apollo`/`urql`/`relay`/`trpc` dependencies.

This is the **`usememos/memos`** project (`module github.com/usememos/memos` in `/bench/repo/go.mod`), a Go backend with a TypeScript/React frontend under `/bench/repo/web`.

## Actual API architecture: Protobuf-defined gRPC + Connect + gRPC-Gateway (REST)

The public API is a **schema-first Protobuf API**. The `.proto` definitions are the single source of truth; Go stubs, a Connect handler, a REST gateway, and an OpenAPI spec are all generated from them.

### Where the API "schema" is actually defined — `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`
The public v1 service contracts (the closest analog to a "public API schema"):
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/attachment_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/instance_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/ai_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/common.proto`
- Design notes: `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/README.md` (follows Google AIPs)
- Codegen config: `/bench/repo/proto/buf.yaml`, `/bench/repo/proto/buf.gen.yaml`

Internal store-layer protos live in `/bench/repo/proto/store/`.

### Generated code — `/bench/repo/proto/gen/`
- gRPC/message stubs: `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.go`, `*_grpc.pb.go`
- REST gateway stubs: `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`
- Connect handlers: `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go`
- **OpenAPI spec (the REST/HTTP schema): `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`** (paths like `/api/v1/...`), embedded via `/bench/repo/proto/openapi_embed.go`

### Server wiring — `/bench/repo/server/`
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go` — builds the **Echo v5** HTTP server (`github.com/labstack/echo/v5`), registers `/healthz`, frontend static files, file server, RSS, the gRPC-Gateway (`apiV1Service.RegisterGateway`), and MCP routes.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` — `RegisterGateway()` mounts both the **gRPC-Gateway** (REST/JSON at `/api/v1/...` via `RegisterXServiceHandlerServer`) and the **Connect** handlers (for browser clients at `/memos.api.v1.*`), plus an SSE endpoint.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go` — Connect handler registration.
- Service implementations: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/*_service.go` (e.g. `memo_service.go`, `user_service.go`, `auth_service.go`, etc.).

### Other HTTP surfaces (`/bench/repo/server/router/`)
- `rss/rss.go` — RSS feeds
- `fileserver/fileserver.go` — file/attachment serving
- `frontend/frontend.go` — serves the built React app
- `mcp/` — a **Model Context Protocol** server (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`), which adapts the same API for LLM tool use (`mcp/service.go`, `mcp/adapter.go`, `mcp/openapi.go`).

### Frontend
`/bench/repo/web` (React/TypeScript) consumes the API via Connect using `@connectrpc/connect` and `@connectrpc/connect-web` (see `/bench/repo/web/package.json`) — again, no GraphQL client.

### Key dependencies (`/bench/repo/go.mod`)
`connectrpc.com/connect`, `github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2`, `google.golang.org/grpc`, `github.com/labstack/echo/v5`, `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`.

**Summary:** No GraphQL exists. The public API is a Protobuf/gRPC API exposed three ways — native gRPC, Connect (for the web client), and a REST/JSON gateway with an auto-generated OpenAPI spec — served through an Echo HTTP server. The authoritative schema is the `.proto` files in `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`, and the REST schema is `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`.
